title: Loss of consortium claims - an underused head of compensation
p1:
A personal injury does not only affect the person who gets hurt.

Sometimes, the biggest loss is felt by the people standing beside them. Yet many people do not even know they can claim compensation for that.
p2:
A common misconception is that compensation only covers medical bills, lost income, or physical pain. But the law may also recognize the loss of companionship, affection, support, and the relationship impact caused by an injury.

This is known as a loss of consortium claim. It focuses on the harm suffered by a spouse or family relationship because of the injured person's condition.
p3:
The surprising part? Two people can experience the same accident, but the financial and emotional consequences can extend far beyond the injured individual. A serious injury can change daily life, responsibilities, and the quality of a relationship.

Knowing about this claim can help families identify compensation avenues they might otherwise overlook.
conclusion: Have you heard of loss of consortium claims before, and do you think people are aware enough about this type of compensation?
